user.name: Roshan
user.goal: Fat loss (4–6 kg cut) with muscle preservation, belly fat reduction, body recomposition

green.summary: Full session — push load with double progression.

yellow.summary: Train as planned but dial back accessories.

red.summary: Recovery is low — light session or rest.

unknown.summary: No Whoop data — train at RIR 3 and stop if performance drops.

adaptation_rules.summary: If workouts change, days are missed, or odd/extra sessions appear, adapt and suggest the plan ahead — do not blindly force the calendar.
principles: Prefer the weekly calendar when training is on track.
On missed days: catch up at most one session, and only if recovery is green — never stack missed days back-to-back.
On odd days (trained on OFF, wrong session type, or unlabeled/New Workout): treat as real work done; shift or lighten the next hard day as needed.
If exercise selection changes in a logged workout, use the latest version as the target and note the change in the plan ahead.

When you swap or add exercises within a session (e.g. T-bar instead of incline row, preacher instead of only incline curls), treat the newest full log as the working template for next time — suggest those lifts and loads, and call out what changed vs the prior version.

Track muscle-part coverage for all major groups inside each session (chest, shoulders, triceps, biceps, back, legs). If one part was under-covered last time, suggest emphasis for that part in the next matching session.
Keep planned movement patterns (squat/hinge/push/pull/arms) but allow exercise variation inside them; do not force old exercises if you replaced them.
After an odd or hard unexpected session, protect the next planned rest day or insert an easier day before the next compounds.
Always show the next several days of suggested sessions so the week stays clear.

nutrition.calorie_awareness: 300-400 kcal deficit daily. Gym days ~1850, rest days ~1650. Never go below 1500 kcal — muscle loss accelerates below that.
nutrition.diet_notes: Eggs, dairy, chicken, goat, vegetables, fruits, nuts, dates, and other staples OK.

carb_strategy.gym_days: Higher carbs — prioritize around training; keep dinner lighter
carb_strategy.off_days: Lighter carbs all day — mostly protein + vegetables
carb_strategy.night_carbs: Minimize rice/roti at dinner; prefer protein + veg at night to reduce belly fat

nutrition.alcohol: Minimize; avoid the night before training when possible

belly_fat_rules.summary: Target: lose 4–6 kg (69 → 63–65 kg) in 12–16 weeks. South Asian visceral fat predisposition — also track waist target 80 cm. Key levers: calorie deficit, sleep, daily steps, resistance training.
rules: Eat ~1850 kcal on gym days, ~1650 kcal on rest days — 300-400 kcal deficit drives fat loss.
Never go below 1500 kcal — muscle loss accelerates and metabolism adapts negatively.
Keep protein at 110 g every day — this is non-negotiable to preserve muscle during cut.
Sleep 7–7.5 h every night — poor sleep raises cortisol which stalls fat loss and drives belly fat storage.
Hit 8000+ steps daily, including rest days — walking burns ~300-400 kcal and is effective for visceral fat.
Keep dinner mostly protein + vegetables; avoid heavy carbs (rice/roti) after 7 PM.
Maintain resistance training 5x/week — lifting preserves muscle mass during calorie deficit.
Manage stress — cortisol spikes store fat preferentially around the belly.
Weigh yourself weekly (same time, morning, fasted) — expect 0.3–0.5 kg/week drop.
Measure waist monthly — target is 80 cm (currently 85 cm).

coaching_reminders.low_sleep: Sleep under 7 h — cortisol will be elevated; belly fat reduction stalls on poor sleep.
coaching_reminders.rest_day: REST DAY: target ~1650 kcal, 110 g protein; hit 8000+ steps; keep dinner light (protein + veg, skip heavy carbs).
coaching_reminders.gym_day: GYM DAY: target ~1850 kcal, 110 g protein; lift hard, walk to/from if possible, lighter carbs at dinner.
coaching_reminders.stress_flag: High stress day logged — prioritize sleep tonight; stress cortisol stores belly fat.
